newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels move southwest towards mining area.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels move southwest towards mining area.

text.p: Hundreds of battle-hardened Banyamulenge rebel troops moved deeper into southeastern Zaire on Saturday in a campaign to capture rich mineral workings in the area.
A convoy of trucks, buses, cars and motorbikes packed with heavily armed rebel troops was on the move near Chimanga, about 100 km (60 miles) southwest of the border town of Bukavu.

Rebel troops patrolling in the area said remnants of the Zairean army they crushed last month were regrouping with former Rwandan army soldiers and Interahamwe militiamen from the abandoned Hutu refugee camp at Chimanga.
"The area is not safe," said one soldier. "There has been a lot of fighting."

In Bukavu, trucks packed with new recruits to the rebel force roared through the streets on Saturday evening. The recruits, mainly ethnic Tutsis -- an important element in the rebel force -- were cheering and singing victory songs.
Those in the convoy headed south were more subdued. Many of them had taken part in heavy fighting earlier this month at Nyabibwe, about 120 km (70 miles) north of Bukavu.

Many of the vehicles in the convoy had been abandoned by the Interahamwe and former Rwandan army when the Zairean rebels, also known as the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, routed them at in that fighting.

One soldier said they were heading for Kamituga, another 60 km (40 miles) beyond Chimanga. They said Zairean troops were preparing to make a stand to protect the rich gold and diamond diggings in the area.
At nearby Chimanga camp, local Red Cross and Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) workers managed to treat for the first time on Saturday survivors of a massacre of more than 300 Hutu refugees.
The rebel authorities had restricted aid organisations to within 30 km (20 miles) of Bukavu but they let a mission through on Saturday after journalists reported the massacre.
The aid workers managed to collect six Hutu refugees -- all seriously injured with bullet wounds -- before rebel troops asked them to leave the area.

Villagers told Reuters earlier this week that the rebels were responsible for the massacre. The rebels had gathered the people who had not fled with the former Rwandan army and the Interahamwe and told them they were to be repatriated, they said.
But instead, witnesses said, rebels lobbed grenades into the gathering and gunned down those who tried to flee.

An MSF doctor managed to treat Marie Nyiratezimana, a young woman who has lain in a maize field for 13 days. Shrapnel wounds had left her left leg in tatters below her knee and she had two bullet wounds in her arm.
They also found another seriously injured man hidden in a pigpen. Both had managed to stay alive after being given rudimentary treatment by local villagers.
One villager said there were over 100 people with shrapnel and bullet wounds hidden in the bush surrounding the camp.
Villagers were clearly terrified of showing where the wounded were while rebel soldiers were present and people relied on furtive signals and eye movement to steer Red Cross workers to the hurt.
Aid officials said they would make another attempt to visit Chimanga on Sunday.
